test_title: PYST 69: SSC CGL 2024 - Quantitative Aptitude (Held On 19 Sept, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: maths
question: The ratio of boys to girls initial in a college is 5 : 6. If 40 boys leave the college and 50 girls join the college, the ratio will become 8 : 11. Find the number of girls (initial) in the college.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Initial Ratio (Boys : Girls) = 5 : 6 | Final Ratio = 8 : 11 | Change = −40 : +50

Equate the difference of the ratio cross-products to the value cross-products:

⇒ |(5 × 11) − (6 × 8)| units = |(8 × 50) − (11 × (−40))|

⇒ 7 units = (400 + 440) = 840 ⇒ 1 unit = 120

⇒ Initial Girls = 6 units = 6 × 120 = 720

**∴ The correct answer is 720 girls.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial ratio of boys to girls = 5 : 6

Boys who left the college = 40

Girls who joined the college = 50

Final ratio of boys to girls = 8 : 11

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/780039068bb6a64ee8793f40cae78649e1d2357657de4aa3a4f1bb93b4b9a449.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the initial number of boys be 5x and the initial number of girls be 6x.

After changes, the new number of boys = 5x − 40

And the new number of girls = 6x + 50

According to the given condition, we equate the new quantities to the final ratio:

⇒ (5x − 40) ÷ (6x + 50) = 8 ÷ 11

⇒ 11 × (5x − 40) = 8 × (6x + 50)

⇒ 55x − 440 = 48x + 400

⇒ 55x − 48x = 400 + 440

⇒ 7x = 840

⇒ x = 120

The initial number of girls = 6x

⇒ 6 × 120 = 720

**∴ The correct answer is 720 girls.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cross-Multiplication Method

Used rapidly when two quantities in a given ratio change by specific amounts to form a new ratio. Equate the difference of the ratio cross-products directly to the difference of the value cross-products.

Compound Ratio

When two or more ratios are multiplied together, it forms a compound ratio. For ratios a:b and c:d, the compound ratio is ac:bd.

Proportion Rule

An equation stating that two ratios are equal is called a proportion. If a ÷ b = c ÷ d, then a × d = b × c (product of extremes equals product of means).
